steps.note: Add the foreign key as NOT VALID: no table scan, so the SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE lock on orders/customers is held only for an instant. From here on every new or updated order must reference an existing customer. Short lock_timeout so the ALTER never queues app INSERTs behind it for long; retry up to 30 times if it cannot get the lock.
steps.sql: DO $$ BEGIN PERFORM set_config('lock_timeout', '300ms', true); FOR i IN 1..30 LOOP BEGIN ALTER TABLE orders ADD CONSTRAINT orders_customer_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (customer_id) REFERENCES customers (id) NOT VALID; RETURN; EXCEPTION WHEN lock_not_available THEN PERFORM pg_sleep(1); END; END LOOP; RAISE EXCEPTION 'could not lock orders/customers to add the foreign key'; END $$;

steps.note: Validate the existing 10M rows. VALIDATE takes only SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE on orders and ROW SHARE on customers, so app reads and inserts keep running during the scan. No statement timeout for this long scan.
steps.sql: SET statement_timeout = 0; SET lock_timeout = '60s'; ALTER TABLE orders VALIDATE CONSTRAINT orders_customer_id_fkey;

steps.note: Check: the constraint exists and is validated (fails the plan otherwise).
steps.sql: DO $$ BEGIN IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint WHERE conname = 'orders_customer_id_fkey' AND conrelid = 'orders'::regclass AND contype = 'f' AND convalidated) THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'orders_customer_id_fkey missing or not validated'; END IF; END $$;
